selectors-declarations-and-rules.label: Selectors, Declarations, and Rules
selectors-declarations-and-rules.summary: Target the right elements with type, class, and descendant selectors, then build valid declaration blocks from properties and values.

try_selectors_declarations_and_rules_ske.title: Try it yourself: Use a type selector across the portfolio
try_selectors_declarations_and_rules_ske.prompt:
**Problem**

Paragraph text appears across several pages, so styling each paragraph individually would repeat the same work.

**Task**

Keep the existing stylesheet and add a `p` type-selector rule with `color: #334155;`.

try_selectors_declarations_and_rules_ske.title: Try it yourself: Use the portfolio's small class hook
try_selectors_declarations_and_rules_ske.prompt:
**Problem**

The Home introduction needs stronger emphasis, but changing every paragraph would also affect ordinary body text. The existing `intro` class gives CSS a precise hook.

**Task**

Keep all previous CSS and add `.intro { font-weight: 600; }`. Do not add new classes to the HTML.

try_selectors_declarations_and_rules_ske.title: Try it yourself: Use a descendant selector for navigation links
try_selectors_declarations_and_rules_ske.prompt:
**Problem**

Navigation links should share one visual treatment, but adding a class to every link would duplicate markup work. Their shared relationship to `nav` already identifies them.

**Task**

Keep the cumulative stylesheet and add `nav a { color: #0f766e; }`.

selector-role-choice.title: Identify the selector
selector-role-choice.hint: It appears before the opening brace and determines what is targeted.

help.concept: Selectors identify which elements a rule targets.
help.hint_1: It appears before the opening brace and determines what is targeted.
help.hint_2: Compare each choice with the rule shown in the lesson.

class-selector-choice.title: Match selectors to reusable targeting jobs
class-selector-choice.prompt: Which statements correctly describe selectors used in the portfolio? Select all that apply.
class-selector-choice.hint: Compare a type selector, a class selector, and a descendant selector by the set of elements each one can actually match.

help.concept: Selector choice should match the scope of the styling job without adding unnecessary markup.
help.hint_1: Type selectors match element names; class selectors match an existing class hook.
help.hint_2: A descendant selector is limited by its ancestor relationship, and type selectors do not need ids.

options.a: A p selector can apply one rule to paragraph elements across the linked pages.
options.b: The .intro selector targets elements that already carry the intro class.
options.c: The selector nav a targets every anchor element anywhere in the document.
options.d: Using an h2 selector requires adding a unique id to every h2 first.

declaration-parts-multi.title: Identify declaration pieces
declaration-parts-multi.prompt: Which are parts of the declaration `color: navy;`?
declaration-parts-multi.hint: Focus on the syntax inside a CSS declaration block.

help.concept: Declarations pair a property with a value.
help.hint_1: Focus on the syntax inside a CSS declaration block.
help.hint_2: Select every choice that matches the lesson, not just one.

options.c: A colon between property and value

rule-reading-order.title: Read a rule in order
rule-reading-order.prompt: Arrange these ideas in the order you encounter them in a simple CSS rule.
rule-reading-order.hint: Read a rule from left to right.

help.concept: A CSS rule wraps declarations in a block after the selector.
help.hint_1: Read a rule from left to right.
help.hint_2: Follow the sequence from targeting an element to seeing the browser render it.

selector-list-fill.title: Name the separator
selector-list-fill.prompt: Choose the punctuation used to make a selector list.
selector-list-fill.hint: Do not confuse a selector list with a descendant selector.

help.concept: Commas separate selectors in a selector list.
help.hint_1: Do not confuse a selector list with a descendant selector.
help.hint_2: Use the exact CSS term introduced in the lesson.

selector-list-fill.template: Use a [blank1] between independent selectors that should share one rule.

descendant-selector-fill.title: Name the relationship selector
descendant-selector-fill.prompt: Complete the statement about the selector `.card p`.
descendant-selector-fill.hint: Look at the space between `.card` and `p`, and think about how the second selector is limited by where the paragraph appears.

help.concept: A selector can narrow a target by requiring one matching element to appear somewhere inside another matching element.
help.hint_1: The paragraph is selected only when it appears inside an element with the `card` class.
help.hint_2: Choose the relationship-based selector name that describes nested matching rather than a selector list, class-only selector, or ID selector.

descendant-selector-fill.template: The selector `.card p` is a [blank1] selector.

rule-anatomy.title: A rule combines a selector with declarations

type-and-class-selectors.title: Type selectors are broad; class selectors are reusable and specific
type-and-class-selectors.bodyMarkdown:
A **type selector** such as `p` targets every matching element of that type. That is useful when you want a site-wide baseline. A **class selector** starts with a dot and targets elements whose HTML `class` attribute contains that class: ```css .intro { font-size: 1.2rem; } ``` ```html

Aspiring web developer.

``` Classes are reusable. Several elements can share the same class, and one element can carry multiple classes. Use a class when the styling represents a reusable role or component rather than every element of one HTML type.
